### Regression tests

Issue #113: EOL character weirdness on Windows
(Important: first line ends with CR + CR + LF)

```````````````````````````````` example
line1

line2
.

├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
│   └── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:5 literal="line1" children=0
└── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=3:1..3:5 children=1
    └── Text id=3:1 scope=3:1..3:5 literal="line2" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Issue #114: markdown_core skipping first character in line
(Important: the blank lines around "Repeatedly" contain a tab.)

```````````````````````````````` example
By taking it apart

- alternative solutions
→
Repeatedly solving
→
- how techniques
.

├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:18 children=1

├── List id=3:0 scope=3:1..4:1 flavor=bullet start=null tight=true children=1
│   └── ListItem id=4:0 scope=3:1..4:1 checked=null children=1
│       └── Paragraph id=5:0 scope=3:3..3:23 children=1
│           └── Text id=5:1 scope=3:3..3:23 literal="alternative solutions" children=0
├── Paragraph id=6:0 scope=5:1..5:18 children=1
│   └── Text id=6:1 scope=5:1..5:18 literal="Repeatedly solving" children=0
└── List id=7:0 scope=7:1..7:16 flavor=bullet start=null tight=true children=1
    └── ListItem id=8:0 scope=7:1..7:16 checked=null children=1
        └── Paragraph id=9:0 scope=7:3..7:16 children=1
            └── Text id=9:1 scope=7:3..7:16 literal="how techniques" children=0
````````````````````````````````

markdown-core strikethrough rules

```````````````````````````````` example strikethrough
~Hi~ Hello, world!
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:18 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:18 children=2
    ├── Strikethrough id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:4 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:3 literal="Hi" children=0
    └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:5..1:18 literal=" Hello, world!" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example strikethrough
This ~text~ ~~is~~ ~~~curious~~~.
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:33 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:33 children=5
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:5 literal="This " children=0
    ├── Strikethrough id=2:2 scope=1:6..1:11 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:7..1:10 literal="text" children=0
    ├── Text id=2:4 scope=1:12..1:12 literal=" " children=0
    ├── Strikethrough id=2:5 scope=1:13..1:18 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:6 scope=1:15..1:16 literal="is" children=0
    └── Text id=2:7 scope=1:19..1:33 literal=" ~~~curious~~~." children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example

.

└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:57 children=1
    └── Link id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:57 destination="http://members.aon.at/~nkehrer/ibm_5110/emu5110.html" title=null children=1
        └── Text id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:2 literal="x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Footnotes may be nested inside other footnotes.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
This is some text. It has a citation.[^citation]

[^another-citation]: My second citation.

[^citation]: This is a long winded parapgraph that also has another citation.[^another-citation]
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..5:96 children=3
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:48 children=2
│   ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:37 literal="This is some text. It has a citation." children=0
│   └── FootnoteReference id=2:2 scope=1:38..1:48 label="citation" definition=5:0 children=0
├── FootnoteDefinition id=3:0 scope=3:1..4:0 label="another-citation" norm="^another-citation" children=1
│   └── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=3:22..3:40 children=1
│       └── Text id=4:1 scope=3:22..3:40 literal="My second citation." children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=5:0 scope=5:1..5:96 label="citation" norm="^citation" children=1
    └── Paragraph id=6:0 scope=5:14..5:96 children=2
        ├── Text id=6:1 scope=5:14..5:77 literal="This is a long winded parapgraph that also has another citation." children=0
        └── FootnoteReference id=6:2 scope=5:78..5:96 label="another-citation" definition=3:0 children=0
````````````````````````````````

Footnotes are similar to, but should not be confused with, link references

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
This is some text. It has two footnotes references, side-by-side without any spaces,[^footnote1][^footnote2] which are definitely not link references.

[^footnote1]: Hello.

[^footnote2]: Goodbye.
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..5:22 children=3
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:150 children=4
│   ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:84 literal="This is some text. It has two footnotes references, side-by-side without any spaces," children=0
│   ├── FootnoteReference id=2:2 scope=1:85..1:96 label="footnote1" definition=3:0 children=0
│   ├── FootnoteReference id=2:3 scope=1:97..1:108 label="footnote2" definition=5:0 children=0
│   └── Text id=2:4 scope=1:109..1:150 literal=" which are definitely not link references." children=0
├── FootnoteDefinition id=3:0 scope=3:1..4:0 label="footnote1" norm="^footnote1" children=1
│   └── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=3:15..3:20 children=1
│       └── Text id=4:1 scope=3:15..3:20 literal="Hello." children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=5:0 scope=5:1..5:22 label="footnote2" norm="^footnote2" children=1
    └── Paragraph id=6:0 scope=5:15..5:22 children=1
        └── Text id=6:1 scope=5:15..5:22 literal="Goodbye." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Footnotes may begin with or have a 'w' or a '_' in their reference label.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes autolink
This is some text. Sometimes the autolinker splits up text into multiple nodes, hoping it will find a hyperlink, so this text has a footnote whose reference label begins with a `w`.[^widely-cited]

It has another footnote that contains many different characters (the autolinker was also breaking on `_`).[^sphinx-of-black-quartz_judge-my-vow-0123456789]

[^sphinx-of-black-quartz_judge-my-vow-0123456789]: so does this.

[^widely-cited]: this renders properly.
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..7:39 children=4
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:196 children=4
│   ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:177 literal="This is some text. Sometimes the autolinker splits up text into multiple nodes, hoping it will find a hyperlink, so this text has a footnote whose reference label begins with a " children=0
│   ├── Code id=2:2 scope=1:178..1:180 literal="w" children=0
│   ├── Text id=2:3 scope=1:181..1:181 literal="." children=0
│   └── FootnoteReference id=2:4 scope=1:182..1:196 label="widely-cited" definition=6:0 children=0
├── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=3:1..3:155 children=4
│   ├── Text id=3:1 scope=3:1..3:101 literal="It has another footnote that contains many different characters (the autolinker was also breaking on " children=0
│   ├── Code id=3:2 scope=3:102..3:104 literal="_" children=0
│   ├── Text id=3:3 scope=3:105..3:106 literal=")." children=0
│   └── FootnoteReference id=3:4 scope=3:107..3:155 label="sphinx-of-black-quartz_judge-my-vow-0123456789" definition=4:0 children=0
├── FootnoteDefinition id=4:0 scope=5:1..6:0 label="sphinx-of-black-quartz_judge-my-vow-0123456789" norm="^sphinx-of-black-quartz_judge-my-vow-0123456789" children=1
│   └── Paragraph id=5:0 scope=5:52..5:64 children=1
│       └── Text id=5:1 scope=5:52..5:64 literal="so does this." children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=6:0 scope=7:1..7:39 label="widely-cited" norm="^widely-cited" children=1
    └── Paragraph id=7:0 scope=7:18..7:39 children=1
        └── Text id=7:1 scope=7:18..7:39 literal="this renders properly." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Footnotes interacting with strikethrough should not lead to a use-after-free.
Since Step 9a nothing defines `_a_`, so this is not a footnote call at all: the
brackets are an unmatched `[`, and the emphasis the core parser built inside
them stays. Upstream flattens the whole span into one literal, which is the
registered `footnote-failed-call-interior` divergence.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes autolink strikethrough table
|Tot.....[^_a_]|
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:16 children=3
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:11 literal="|Tot.....[^" children=0
    ├── Emphasis id=2:2 scope=1:12..1:14 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:13..1:13 literal="a" children=0
    └── Text id=2:4 scope=1:15..1:16 literal="]|" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Footnotes interacting with strikethrough should not lead to a use-after-free, pt2.
Same rule as above, with a strikethrough as the interior.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes autolink strikethrough table
[^~~is~~1]
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:10 children=3
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:2 literal="[^" children=0
    ├── Strikethrough id=2:2 scope=1:3..1:8 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:5..1:6 literal="is" children=0
    └── Text id=2:4 scope=1:9..1:10 literal="1]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Adjacent unused footnote definitions should not lead to a use after free -- and
since Step 9a they are KEPT rather than dropped, so this example also pins that
a definition nothing refers to is still a node, and that a definition written
inside another one stays inside it.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes autolink strikethrough table
Hello world


[^a]:[^b]:
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..4:10 children=2
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:11 children=1
│   └── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:11 literal="Hello world" children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=3:0 scope=4:1..4:10 label="a" norm="^a" children=1
    └── FootnoteDefinition id=4:0 scope=4:6..4:10 label="b" norm="^b" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Issue #424 - emphasis before links

```````````````````````````````` example
*text* [link](#section)
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:23 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:23 children=3
    ├── Emphasis id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:6 children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:5 literal="text" children=0
    ├── Text id=2:3 scope=1:7..1:7 literal=" " children=0
    └── Link id=2:4 scope=1:8..1:23 destination="#section" title=null children=1
        └── Text id=2:5 scope=1:9..1:12 literal="link" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A footnote call whose label crosses a line ending keeps its bytes

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
x[^a
b] tail
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:7 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:7 children=3
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:4 literal="x[^a" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak id=2:2 scope=1:5..1:5 children=0
    └── Text id=2:3 scope=2:1..2:7 literal="b] tail" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An entity-spelled caret is read out of the source, not out of a freed node.
Recognition is a question about the SOURCE, so this opens no call at all and the
entity simply decodes; before 0a.9 it opened one and came back as
`x [^Hat;abcdefghij] y`, with the caret invented and the entity's own bytes left
in the label.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
x [&Hat;abcdefghij] y

[^z]: note
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..3:10 children=2
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:21 children=1
│   └── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:21 literal="x [^abcdefghij] y" children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=3:0 scope=3:1..3:10 label="z" norm="^z" children=1
    └── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=3:7..3:10 children=1
        └── Text id=4:1 scope=3:7..3:10 literal="note" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An escaped caret opens no call and does not manufacture a closing bracket. `\^`
is an escaped punctuation character, so the text is one caret; before 0a.9 this
came back as `[^^abc] x`, with a second caret invented, and before 0a.2 as
`[^abc]] x`, with a bracket nobody wrote.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
[\^abc] x
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
    └── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:9 literal="[^abc] x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Recognition depends on the raw source byte and on nothing else, and a matching
definition does not change that. This is the 432-case matrix reduced: six caret
spellings against one label, with the definition present. Only the raw caret is
a call, so exactly one FootnoteReference appears and the definition resolves to
it; the other five decode to the identical text and open nothing. The six are
separate paragraphs rather than one, so the example adds no SoftBreak sentinels
to specs/scope-sanity/ledger.json, which is a ratchet that only shrinks.

The full matrix is six caret spellings x eight labels x three tails x three
definition contexts. 360 of the 432 move at 0a.9, and the split is exactly the
caret: all 72 raw-caret cases are untouched, and all 72 of each of the five
other spellings move. The label and tail dimensions never affect the decision,
which is why the fixture drops them.

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
a[^n] b

a[\^n] b

a[&#94;n] b

a[&#x5E;n] b

a[&#x5e;n] b

a[&Hat;n] b

[^n]: note
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..13:10 children=7
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:7 children=3
│   ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:1 literal="a" children=0
│   ├── FootnoteReference id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:5 label="n" definition=8:0 children=0
│   └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:6..1:7 literal=" b" children=0
├── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=3:1..3:8 children=1
│   └── Text id=3:1 scope=3:1..3:8 literal="a[^n] b" children=0
├── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=5:1..5:11 children=1
│   └── Text id=4:1 scope=5:1..5:11 literal="a[^n] b" children=0
├── Paragraph id=5:0 scope=7:1..7:12 children=1
│   └── Text id=5:1 scope=7:1..7:12 literal="a[^n] b" children=0
├── Paragraph id=6:0 scope=9:1..9:12 children=1
│   └── Text id=6:1 scope=9:1..9:12 literal="a[^n] b" children=0
├── Paragraph id=7:0 scope=11:1..11:11 children=1
│   └── Text id=7:1 scope=11:1..11:11 literal="a[^n] b" children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=8:0 scope=13:1..13:10 label="n" norm="^n" children=1
    └── Paragraph id=9:0 scope=13:7..13:10 children=1
        └── Text id=9:1 scope=13:7..13:10 literal="note" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A footnote definition nested inside a duplicate of itself keeps both

```````````````````````````````` example footnotes
Ref [^dup].

[^dup]: OUTER opens first

    [^dup]: INNER closes first
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..5:30 children=2
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:11 children=3
│   ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:4 literal="Ref " children=0
│   ├── FootnoteReference id=2:2 scope=1:5..1:10 label="dup" definition=3:0 children=0
│   └── Text id=2:3 scope=1:11..1:11 literal="." children=0
└── FootnoteDefinition id=3:0 scope=3:1..5:30 label="dup" norm="^dup" children=2
    ├── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=3:9..3:25 children=1
    │   └── Text id=4:1 scope=3:9..3:25 literal="OUTER opens first" children=0
    └── FootnoteDefinition id=5:0 scope=5:5..5:30 label="dup" norm="^dup" children=1
        └── Paragraph id=6:0 scope=5:13..5:30 children=1
            └── Text id=6:1 scope=5:13..5:30 literal="INNER closes first" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An autolink inside a block quote contains its own text. Its columns used to
come from a raw subject-buffer offset with neither the container's block offset
nor the line's column offset added, so the Link and the Text it holds were
computed in two different coordinate spaces and the child escaped the parent.
cmark-gfm reports the same wrong columns, so upstream sourcepos cannot be the
oracle here.

```````````````````````````````` example autolink
> see <https://x.example/> ok
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..1:29 children=1
└── BlockQuote id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:29 children=1
    └── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=1:3..1:29 children=3
        ├── Text id=3:1 scope=1:3..1:6 literal="see " children=0
        ├── Link id=3:2 scope=1:7..1:26 destination="https://x.example/" title=null children=1
        │   └── Text id=3:3 scope=1:8..1:25 literal="https://x.example/" children=0
        └── Text id=3:4 scope=1:27..1:29 literal=" ok" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The same defect on a continuation line, where the missing term is the column
offset rather than the block offset.

```````````````````````````````` example autolink
lead
see <https://x.example/> ok
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:27 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:27 children=5
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:4 literal="lead" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak id=2:2 scope=1:5..1:5 children=0
    ├── Text id=2:3 scope=2:1..2:4 literal="see " children=0
    ├── Link id=2:4 scope=2:5..2:24 destination="https://x.example/" title=null children=1
    │   └── Text id=2:5 scope=2:6..2:23 literal="https://x.example/" children=0
    └── Text id=2:6 scope=2:25..2:27 literal=" ok" children=0
````````````````````````````````

THIS EXAMPLE PINS A DEFECT (D27), and the row below is the wrong answer.

A node's scope covers its literal: `a <b c> d` gives `HTML scope=1:3..1:7` for
five bytes of tag. When the same tag crosses a line ending the end column is one
short — `2:1` below, where the `>` is at column 2 — so the closing byte belongs
to no node while the text after it is placed correctly at `2:3`. The cause is
the span handed to `adjust_subj_node_newlines`: raw HTML passes `matchlen` with
an `extra` of 1, which omits the tag's last byte from the newline count, and the
same `extra` makes the following node's column right. cmark-gfm is wrong the
same way, so fixing it is a deliberate divergence and belongs to Step 8's
position model, not to a defect commit that would have to decide it in passing.
Unpinning this row is that step's gate.

```````````````````````````````` example
a <b
c> d
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:4 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:4 children=3
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:2 literal="a " children=0
    ├── HTML id=2:2 scope=1:3..2:2 literal="<b\nc>" children=0
    └── Text id=2:3 scope=2:3..2:4 literal=" d" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A code span that crosses a line ending inside a block quote ends at a column of
the SOURCE line, not of the container's stripped content. `since_newline` counts
from the start of the content, which begins at column 3 here, so the block
offset has to be added back. Without it the span ends at 2:1 and every gate in
this repository stays green, which is why this example exists.

```````````````````````````````` example
> a `x
> y` b
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:6 children=1
└── BlockQuote id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:6 children=1
    └── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=1:3..2:6 children=3
        ├── Text id=3:1 scope=1:3..1:4 literal="a " children=0
        ├── Code id=3:2 scope=1:5..2:4 literal="x y" children=0
        └── Text id=3:3 scope=2:5..2:6 literal=" b" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A definition's title candidate followed by non-whitespace is un-read: the
rewind puts the position back before it, the bytes stay paragraph text, and the
definition has no title. The scanned chunk used to go into the reference map
anyway, so a reference to the label resolved with a title the definition does
not have — and the same bytes were stated twice, once as prose and once as a
title. The CommonMark specification's own prose for this construct says "this
is a link reference definition, but it has no title". cmark-gfm keeps the
title; that divergence is registered as `refdef-title-rewind`.

The first paragraph's position is D18: the definition was consumed off its
front, and it used to keep the definition's line and column. 0a.12 fixed the
line and left the column to Q22, which requirement 10 then answered from the
content-to-source map. NEITHER ROW MOVED THERE, and this paragraph used to
predict that both would: the definition's line and the surviving line have the
same stripped prefix here, so the column D18 declined to touch was already
right. The input that separates them is the last example in this file, and it
had to be written because no existing one could tell the two rules apart.

```````````````````````````````` example
[foo]: /url
"title" ok

[foo]
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..4:5 children=3
├── ReferenceDefinition id=3:0 scope=1:1..1:11 label="foo" norm="foo" destination="/url" title=null children=0
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=2:1..2:10 children=1
│   └── Text id=2:1 scope=2:1..2:10 literal="\"title\" ok" children=0
└── Paragraph id=4:0 scope=4:1..4:5 children=1
    └── LinkReference id=4:1 scope=4:1..4:5 label="foo" form=shortcut definition=3:0 children=1
        └── Text id=4:2 scope=4:2..4:4 literal="foo" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A link begins at its own opening bracket. It used to take its start line from
the CLOSING bracket, so a link whose label crosses a line ending began after its
own first child — `Link 2:1..2:6` around a `Text` at `1:2`. That half of D19 has
no other witness in this repository: reverting it alone leaves `correctness`
67/67 and all three position oracles green, and only this example plus
`scripts/audit-scope-containment.mjs`'s sibling/parent rule catches it.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a
b](/u) tail
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:11 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:11 children=2
    ├── Link id=2:1 scope=1:1..2:6 destination="/u" title=null children=3
    │   ├── Text id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:2 literal="a" children=0
    │   ├── SoftBreak id=2:3 scope=1:3..1:3 children=0
    │   └── Text id=2:4 scope=2:1..2:1 literal="b" children=0
    └── Text id=2:5 scope=2:7..2:11 literal=" tail" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A reference definition consumed off the front of a paragraph leaves the
paragraph starting on a later line — and, where the surviving line's stripped
prefix differs from the definition's, in a different column. D18 corrected the
line and left the column with a note that it was right in every corpus case,
which was true and is why nothing here caught it: this input is the missing
one. Lazily continuing a block quote strips two bytes from the definition's
line and none from the paragraph's, so the paragraph used to begin at column 3
of a line whose first byte is at column 1 — starting after its own only child,
which `scripts/audit-scope-containment.mjs` also sees. Requirement 10 answers
both coordinates from the content-to-source map instead of counting line
endings and leaving the column alone.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [a]: /x
bar
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:3 children=1
└── BlockQuote id=2:0 scope=1:1..2:3 children=2
    ├── ReferenceDefinition id=4:0 scope=1:3..1:9 label="a" norm="a" destination="/x" title=null children=0
    └── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=2:1..2:3 children=1
        └── Text id=3:1 scope=2:1..2:3 literal="bar" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Two link reference definitions in one paragraph, the second one indented. The
indentation ahead of a definition's opening bracket belongs to the block's
PARENT, which is where the FIRST line's indentation already went, before the
block existed to claim it. Giving it to either definition puts a region outside
its owner's scope — before the second one's bracket, after the first one's last
byte — and `scripts/audit-concrete-records.mjs` says so. NOTHING ELSE DOES:
with the rule reversed, `correctness` reads 69/69 and every ledger holds,
because no other fixture has two definitions in one paragraph with the second
one indented.

```````````````````````````````` example
  [a]: /1
  [b]: /2
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..2:9 children=2
├── ReferenceDefinition id=2:0 scope=1:3..1:9 label="a" norm="a" destination="/1" title=null children=0
└── ReferenceDefinition id=4:0 scope=2:3..2:9 label="b" norm="b" destination="/2" title=null children=0
````````````````````````````````

Three link reference definitions and a paragraph, all in ONE region. Regions
are laid down left to right and merged when owner, role and cursor line up, so
consecutive unindented definitions with prose after them are a SINGLE region
that has to be cut into four. The cut is counted first, the array grown once
and the surviving rows right-aligned inside the window they will occupy, so the
forward fill can never overtake its own source; dropping the right-alignment
SEGFAULTS on this input. No other fixture reaches the arithmetic: every other
multi-definition case in this repository indents at least one of them, and an
indent breaks the merge.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a]: /1
[b]: /2
[c]: /3
x
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..4:1 children=4
├── ReferenceDefinition id=3:0 scope=1:1..1:7 label="a" norm="a" destination="/1" title=null children=0
├── ReferenceDefinition id=4:0 scope=2:1..2:7 label="b" norm="b" destination="/2" title=null children=0
├── ReferenceDefinition id=5:0 scope=3:1..3:7 label="c" norm="c" destination="/3" title=null children=0
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=4:1..4:1 children=1
    └── Text id=2:1 scope=4:1..4:1 literal="x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A LABEL DEFINED TWICE. The first definition wins the label and the second one
resolves nothing — and both are nodes that own their own bytes, which is
requirement 11c's second sentence. Upstream keeps neither: it consumes both
into a map and frees the paragraph they were written in.
`audit-concrete-records.mjs`'s L5 is what says they own them, and it covers
`ReferenceDefinition` and `FootnoteDefinition` for exactly this reason — no
other block kind is checked there, because a container block's bytes are its
children's by construction.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a]: /1
[a]: /2

[a]
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..4:3 children=3
├── ReferenceDefinition id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:7 label="a" norm="a" destination="/1" title=null children=0
├── ReferenceDefinition id=4:0 scope=2:1..2:7 label="a" norm="a" destination="/2" title=null children=0
└── Paragraph id=5:0 scope=4:1..4:3 children=1
    └── LinkReference id=5:1 scope=4:1..4:3 label="a" form=shortcut definition=2:0 children=1
        └── Text id=5:2 scope=4:2..4:2 literal="a" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A REJECTED TABLE LEAVES THE PARAGRAPH WHOLE. The delimiter row's column count
does not match the header row's, so the paragraph stays a paragraph and every
line of it reads as prose -- alongside the unresolved reference, which
CommonMark defines as prose too.

```````````````````````````````` example
see [x][nope] here
| a | b |
| --- |
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..3:7 children=1
└── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..3:7 children=5
    ├── Text id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:18 literal="see [x][nope] here" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak id=2:2 scope=1:19..1:19 children=0
    ├── Text id=2:3 scope=2:1..2:9 literal="| a | b |" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak id=2:4 scope=2:10..2:10 children=0
    └── Text id=2:5 scope=3:1..3:7 literal="| --- |" children=0
````````````````````````````````

REQUIREMENT 14, EVERY ARM OF IT ON ONE PAGE. `null` means the source did not
write this and `""` means it wrote it and it was empty, and before Step 14 the
two shared one representation -- a chunk with a NULL pointer -- which three
separate reads then folded. The corpus could see almost none of it: one
`title=""` row existed in the whole repository and it was in a canonical-AST
fixture, `source=""` appeared nowhere, and `destination=null` was what the dump
printed for `[a]()`.

A destination is REQUIRED (Q26): the empty parentheses ARE the destination the
author wrote. A title is OPTIONAL and both answers are reachable. Neither
parity oracle can see any of this -- `scripts/lib/upstream-cmark.mjs` folds `""`
to `null` on both sides before comparing, for every field but `literal` -- so
these rows are the only gate there is.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a]() [b](<>) [c](/u) [d](/u "") [e](/u "t")

![f]() ![g](<>) ![h](/s "") ![i](/s "t")

[j]: <>
[k]: <> ""
[l]: /u "t"
.
Document id=1:0 scope=1:1..7:11 children=5
├── Paragraph id=2:0 scope=1:1..1:44 children=9
│   ├── Link id=2:1 scope=1:1..1:5 destination="" title=null children=1
│   │   └── Text id=2:2 scope=1:2..1:2 literal="a" children=0
│   ├── Text id=2:3 scope=1:6..1:6 literal=" " children=0
│   ├── Link id=2:4 scope=1:7..1:13 destination="" title=null children=1
│   │   └── Text id=2:5 scope=1:8..1:8 literal="b" children=0
│   ├── Text id=2:6 scope=1:14..1:14 literal=" " children=0
│   ├── Link id=2:7 scope=1:15..1:21 destination="/u" title=null children=1
│   │   └── Text id=2:8 scope=1:16..1:16 literal="c" children=0
│   ├── Text id=2:9 scope=1:22..1:22 literal=" " children=0
│   ├── Link id=2:10 scope=1:23..1:32 destination="/u" title="" children=1
│   │   └── Text id=2:11 scope=1:24..1:24 literal="d" children=0
│   ├── Text id=2:12 scope=1:33..1:33 literal=" " children=0
│   └── Link id=2:13 scope=1:34..1:44 destination="/u" title="t" children=1
│       └── Text id=2:14 scope=1:35..1:35 literal="e" children=0
├── Paragraph id=3:0 scope=3:1..3:40 children=7
│   ├── Image id=3:1 scope=3:1..3:6 source="" title=null children=1
│   │   └── Text id=3:2 scope=3:3..3:3 literal="f" children=0
│   ├── Text id=3:3 scope=3:7..3:7 literal=" " children=0
│   ├── Image id=3:4 scope=3:8..3:15 source="" title=null children=1
│   │   └── Text id=3:5 scope=3:10..3:10 literal="g" children=0
│   ├── Text id=3:6 scope=3:16..3:16 literal=" " children=0
│   ├── Image id=3:7 scope=3:17..3:27 source="/s" title="" children=1
│   │   └── Text id=3:8 scope=3:19..3:19 literal="h" children=0
│   ├── Text id=3:9 scope=3:28..3:28 literal=" " children=0
│   └── Image id=3:10 scope=3:29..3:40 source="/s" title="t" children=1
│       └── Text id=3:11 scope=3:31..3:31 literal="i" children=0
├── ReferenceDefinition id=4:0 scope=5:1..5:7 label="j" norm="j" destination="" title=null children=0
├── ReferenceDefinition id=6:0 scope=6:1..6:10 label="k" norm="k" destination="" title="" children=0
└── ReferenceDefinition id=7:0 scope=7:1..7:11 label="l" norm="l" destination="/u" title="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````
